findings.where: report.md A5 item 1 (lines 527-529) with A1 item 3 (lines 404-407); compare section 4 group 1 (lines 187-188)
findings.what: A5 item 1 gives the owner only one route for the numbers compare_shap.py did not write: take them from A (= B). Those numbers are fire's main-row treeroute top 3 and own-history share [CI], and the sign-agreement intervals. The other route is to correct compare_shap.py and re-run the comparisons, so that the official files hold these numbers. The addendum drops it, although the reconciler's own group-1 text names it and the reconcile skeptic's fix names it for the sign agreement. The protocol bears on the choice. Section 9 defines the comparison's outputs as the compare\ aggregates (AW3_table.md, AW4_table.md, AW4_main_row.json, ...). Section 10 makes S3.13 'the AW3 tables per problem-lead ... (pairs x statistics with intervals ...)'. Only for B1 does section 10 ('Who computes') give the numbers to A and B. Values taken from V\A\results.json would sit outside section 9's files, so S3.13 would no longer equal the AW3/AW4 files. The proposal also does not tell the owner that three of the intervals it takes over are thin: on fire's variable level, rival_ridge|treeroute rests on 64 finite draws of 2,000 (full-sample value undefined), rival_lgbm|treeroute on 1,140 and rival_rf|treeroute on 1,380, and all three are [0, 1]. Spec C21 leaves open the fewest finite replicates for which an interval is given, and compare_shap made no choice there because it evaluated no draw.
findings.evidence: report.md line 187-188: 'To fill fire's row, use A's (= B's) values or run a corrected compare_shap'. skeptic_reconcile.json (sign agreement): 'the interval must come from A/B or from a corrected compare_shap.py'. A5 item 1: 'Proposed: S3.13 and the main row take them from A (= B) and say so.' PROTOCOL.md section 9 lines 540-542; section 10 lines 553-556 and 605-607. A's results.json: problems/fire/levels/variable/pairs/rival_ridge|treeroute/sign_agreement = null, [0, 1], n_finite 64; rival_lgbm|treeroute 1 [0, 1] n 1,140; rival_rf|treeroute 1 [0, 1] n 1,380 (B the same). Spec C21: 'the fewest finite replicates for which an interval is given'.
findings.fix: In A5 item 1, list both options with their consequences. (a) A (= B): disclosed in the paper and recorded in PROTOCOL.md section 14; S3.13 then differs from the compare\ files. (b) Fix compare_shap.py: write fire's top 3 and own-history share outside 'if tr and rivals:' and evaluate the sign agreement on the draws; re-run the comparisons, record it in section 14 and re-check the changed cells against A (= B). Add the three thin fire intervals and ask how they are to be printed.
